title: Finite-state serial output is polynomial-time computable
statement: Let $\sigma$ be a finite set with decidable equality, let $\delta:\sigma\times\{0,1\}^2\to\sigma$ be a state transition function, let $o:\sigma\times\{0,1\}^2\to\{0,1\}$ be an output function, and fix an initial state $s\in\sigma$. For each bit string $z$, decode its two components, pad them on the right with zeros as needed, and form $|z|+2$ ordered pairs of bits. Starting from $s$, apply $o$ to the current state and each successive bit pair to produce the output bit, then update the state using $\delta$; the resulting bit-string function is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: Equality on the state type is decidable

An output function from a state and two bits to a bit
